lines: Host and guest: founder of a 12-person remote design studio
slides.narration: Welcome back to Small Teams. My guest today runs a fully remote design studio of twelve people. Why did you go remote?
slides.speaker: Host

lines: Host and guest: founder of a 12-person remote design studio
slides.narration: Honestly, it started with hiring. Our best candidate lived four time zones away, and we did not want to lose her.
slides.speaker: Guest

lines: Host and guest: founder of a 12-person remote design studio
slides.speaker: Host

lines: Host and guest: founder of a 12-person remote design studio
slides.narration: Decisions. In an office you decide in the hallway. Remotely, we had to write every decision down in a shared log, with a date and an owner.
slides.speaker: Guest

lines: Host and guest: founder of a 12-person remote design studio
slides.speaker: Host

lines: Host and guest: founder of a 12-person remote design studio
slides.narration: For the first month, yes. After that it was faster, because nobody had to ask the same question twice. We now meet in person twice a year.
slides.speaker: Guest

lines: Host and guest: founder of a 12-person remote design studio
slides.narration: Write it down, and meet twice a year. Thanks for joining us.
slides.speaker: Host
